visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with short brown hair wearing a pink hoodie stands in a studio setting, holding a pack of rice paper while talking directly to the camera. (2) Close-up shots show hands cracking two eggs into a glass bowl, then pouring milk and adding sugar to create a custard mixture. (3) The mixture is whisked manually with a wire whisk until smooth and yellow. (4) A round sheet of rice paper is dipped into a yellow egg wash in a white plate until fully coated. (5) The wet rice paper is placed on a brown cutting board and cut into three triangles using pink scissors. (6) The pieces are folded and rolled into a tapered crescent shape resembling a croissant. (7) The rolls are placed in an air fryer basket lined with white parchment paper. (8) Black sesame seeds are sprinkled on top of the rolls. (9) The air fryer control panel displays '180' degrees and is adjusted to '15' minutes. (10) Through the viewing window of the air fryer, the rolls are seen expanding and turning golden brown in a time-lapse sequence. (11) The woman holds a wooden plate of the finished, crispy golden-brown croissants. (12) She takes a large bite, showing the chewy, layered interior while reacting positively.

(3) Crisp rustling of plastic rice paper packaging followed by soft wet splashing sounds as sheets are dipped into the liquid. (4) Distinct rhythmic metallic snips from scissors cutting through the wet material. (5) Gentle thudding and folding noises as the rolls are formed on the cutting board. (6) Mechanical clicks of air fryer buttons followed by the sliding sound and hollow thud of the basket closing. (7) High-pitched beeping tones precede a consistent broadband fan hum during the cooking time-lapse sequence. narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to test a viral internet food hack—making croissants using Vietnamese rice paper—while subtly promoting a Philips air fryer by demonstrating its 'see-through' cooking feature and effectiveness.
